title: Turning curriculum chaos into a Week 1 operating spine
subtitle: A real-world curriculum planning pass showing how CANONICAL turns scattered planning, documents, tasks, classroom posts, and evidence routines into one usable teaching system.

problem.title: The problem
problem.body: A program lead needed an upcoming youth trades / pre-apprenticeship cohort prepared without losing context across files, tools, lesson plans, task lists, print needs, and evidence requirements. The cohort goal existed on paper—a foundations week, a likely capstone direction, safety and verification culture—but it was not yet something an instructor could run from on day one. Too much lived in memory, scattered notes, and "we'll figure it out Monday."

canonicalMove.title: The CANONICAL move
canonicalMove.body: Instead of building one more app, the work was organized into a durable operating spine: a planning anchor, week overview, four daily instructor run sheets, student activity sheets, print queue, task batch, classroom post drafts, and missing-items tracker. The machine room can be complex; the handrail stays simple. Every artifact knows whether it is for students, instructors, classroom, print, or task tracking.

cohortContext.title: Cohort context (generalized)
items: Youth trades / pre-apprenticeship program, Week 1 — Foundations
Four instruction days (Monday through Thursday), full-day shop and classroom rhythm
Working capstone assumption: RV/camper electrical or solar install under supervision—not confirmed on day one, but Week 1 habits connect to that finish line
Week 1 goal: safe shop habits, program systems, evidence routines, and verification culture before capstone-level electrical work

weekPurpose.title: Week 1 purpose
weekPurpose.body: Week 1 establishes how the cohort works: safe shop habits, program systems, evidence routines, and verification culture. Students should leave knowing how to work safely and ask for help without shame, where tools and assignments live, how to upload evidence with correct naming, and that "I think so" is not enough—verification is normal professional behavior. Week 1 is not about proving expertise. It is about building a shared standard: stop when unsure, check before trusting, document what you verified.

evidenceSystem.title: Evidence and verification system
evidenceSystem.body: Week 1 treats documentation as part of safety—not paperwork theater. Students practice a consistent naming pattern, upload through classroom workflows, and use verification logs for trace and measurement work.
namingNotes: Cohort and week/day codes keep files sortable across the program
Mastery check codes tie evidence to skills—not vibes
Student identifier uses initials or ID policy, never full roster dumps on public systems
Date stamp supports audit and instructor review queues
verificationPrinciples: Hints are not proof—meter, trace, or documented check required
Previous owner wiring is not automatically bad—it must be verified
Stop-work authority is normalized, not punitive

phases.label: Before the cohort week
steps: Align on planning anchor—capstone direction, risks, verification culture
Create prep tasks from the task batch
Execute print queue—student handouts and Day 1 materials first
Post week overview and Day 1 classroom draft

phases.label: Each instruction day
steps: Run that day's daily ops sheet from arrival through closeout
Issue activity sheets matching the day's lab stations
Capture evidence during the evidence window—not as an afterthought
Complete instructor closeout checklist before leaving shop

phases.label: End of Week 1
steps: Open questions captured for Week 2 planning
Review evidence naming compliance across the cohort
Hand off week state via index + task queue—not instructor memory

whatChanged.title: What changed
whatChanged.body: The work became findable, teachable, reviewable, printable, and easier to hand off. Daily rhythm, verification habits, and documentation expectations live in one place instead of in someone's head. An instructor can open the week index, pick today's run sheet, print the right activity sheets, post the classroom draft, and close out with a checklist—without reconstructing the system from scratch.

whyItMatters.title: Why it matters
whyItMatters.body: The instructor no longer has to hold the whole system in memory. The structure becomes an external memory hook—reducing friction while preserving judgment and human authority. Technology should not make the user feel tested; it should absorb complexity, reduce shame, make the next step obvious, and leave the user feeling more capable than before they opened it.

principle.title: The principle
principle.body: The system carries the complexity so the user can carry the intention. Verification beats confidence. Documentation is part of safety—not paperwork theater. Hints are not proof.

sections.closing: CANONICAL is project memory, curriculum systems, and AI workflow infrastructure arranged into one coherent working spine. This field proof is category-level documentation only—no private curriculum packets, student data, or unpublished internal files are exposed here.
